interpretation.rate: Sinus rhythm with gradual deceleration at ~91 bpm (range 80–102). HR decelerated progressively from 102→80 bpm. Compared to guitar recording (avg 101 bpm, earlier), raga produced a significantly lower trough rate and clear downward trend.
interpretation.rhythm: Regular sinus rhythm with physiologic rate variation. No ectopic beats.
interpretation.p_waves: Upright in I, II, aVF. Inverted in aVR. Normal sinus P waves.
interpretation.qrs_complex: Narrow (86ms). Good R-wave progression V1→V5. No BBB.
interpretation.st_segments: Isoelectric in all leads. No ST elevation or depression.
interpretation.t_waves: Upright in I, II, III, aVF, V3–V6. Inverted in aVR. Normal.
notable_findings: Progressive heart rate deceleration 102→80 bpm during raga stimulus
Lowest trough rate 80 bpm — consistent with parasympathetic/relaxation response
Slight baseline artifact at recording end (4710 — electrode movement)
Clinically: raga induced measurable cardiac slowing vs baseline
interpretation.overall_assessment: Sinus rhythm with progressive deceleration during Indian classical raga music. HR dropped from 102 to 80 bpm over ~90 seconds, consistent with a parasympathetic/relaxation autonomic response to the raga stimulus.
